To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic alcohol intake in rats induces biochemical, histologic, and functional alterations of the retina.

the retinoid X receptor (RXR) agonist LG100268 is able to reverse the retinal changes induced by chronic alcohol feeding in rats and that this effect is associated with the activation of the retinoic acid receptor (RAR) signaling pathway.

1) the retina is susceptible to the effects of alcohol; 2) chronic alcohol feeding induces biochemical and histological alterations in the retina; 3) chronic alcohol feeding causes retinal degeneration; 4) chronic alcohol feeding impairs retinal function; 5) chronic alcohol feeding increases the risk of developing alcohol-induced retinopathy.

the effects of alcohol on the retina, with special emphasis on the biochemical and functional changes.
